name: Melting point
question: The temperature where each one turns to liquid.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: Mercury is the only metal that's liquid at room temperature.

items.name: Ice
items.fact: Salt lowers the melting point of ice, which is why roads are salted.

items.name: Cocoa butter (chocolate)
items.fact: Chocolate is designed to melt just below body temperature.

items.name: Sodium
items.fact: Sodium melts just below the boiling point of water.

items.name: Sulfur
items.fact: Melted sulfur turns blood red as it heats up.

items.name: Tin
items.fact: Tin's low melting point made it ideal for solder.

items.name: Lead
items.fact: Lead melts at a temperature you can reach on a camping stove.

items.name: Zinc
items.fact: Zinc coats steel to stop it rusting (galvanizing).

items.name: Aluminium
items.fact: Aluminium was once more valuable than gold.

items.name: Table salt
items.fact: Molten salt is used to store heat in some solar power plants.

items.name: Silver
items.fact: Silver conducts electricity and heat better than any other metal.

items.name: Gold
items.fact: All the gold ever mined would fit in a cube about 22 m on each side.

items.name: Copper
items.fact: Copper melts only about 20 °C above gold.

items.name: Iron
items.fact: Iron is the most common element on Earth by mass.

items.name: Titanium
items.fact: Titanium is as strong as some steels but about 45% lighter.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, which made it ideal for light-bulb filaments.
